title: The Stake Was There First
logline: On sixty-four acres of laterite under old coconut, a small government station grows betel the way the district grows it, in sunken beds where a dead or living stake is driven in weeks before the cutting that will climb it, and every bed in the place is a countable list of separate supports that arrived in a fixed order and cannot stand in for one another.
human_question: If the thing holding something up was put there before it, and needs nothing from it in return, what is actually leaning on what?

place.what_kind_of_place: A research station of about sixty-four acres in the interior coconut lowland: an office block, a store, and behind them field after field of betel grown under old coconut on red laterite and clay loam. The unit of the place is the sunken bed, a little over a metre wide and seven or eight metres long, dug below the level of the path so that water stands in it and manure stays put. Down each bed runs a double row of stakes at about a hand-and-a-half's spacing, some of them cut poles of durable dead wood, some of them living cuttings of a quick-growing leguminous tree that roots where it is driven in and puts out its own leaves. At the foot of each stake, two cuttings of betel, not seed: a piece of an older vine, with its own short reserve of strength and nothing else. Over a newly planted bed, coconut fronds or shade netting for a month or six weeks. Along the paths, a hose or a watering can, a heap of cattle manure, a heap of lopped green branches, and small painted boards with plot numbers and treatment names on them, because much of what is planted here is planted in order to find out what one support is worth when the others are held constant. Beyond the station fence, the same crop again on smaller plots all through the district, grown the same way, cut every second or third week for market.
place.why_it_is_worth_watching: Because the whole argument is already on the ground, counted and labelled, and it is beautiful before it means anything. From height in the first light, the old coconut reads as a canopy with a geometry under it: thousands of straight stakes in ruled beds, the light coming down between the palms in bars, the shade cloth over the new plantings pale against the red soil. At eye level the place gives the single clearest image the concept has anywhere. A stake stands in an empty bed for weeks, doing nothing, waiting; the vine that is later planted at its foot cannot stand up at all without it; and when the vine is finally up and heavy with leaf, the stake is exactly as it was, and needs nothing from the vine whatever. The support runs one way and only one way, and you can see it. Then the station adds the other half for nothing: the same tree that is holding a vine up is lopped, and its green branches are laid in the bed as manure, so one thing is plainly helping in two different ways at once. And nothing is a metaphor: it is a crop, on a schedule, with a research board beside it.
place.what_moves_or_changes: Slowly, and in a fixed order that cannot be run backwards. The stake goes in first, alone. The cutting goes in at its foot. The shade goes over both and comes off after four to six weeks. Water and manure arrive, and keep arriving, all year, for years. The vine puts out a leaf every few days and climbs. Every second or third week the mature lower leaves are taken, so the vine is always being shortened from below while it lengthens above. A stake rots and is replaced under a standing vine. The leguminous supports are cut back when they shade too much, and their loppings go into the bed. Nothing in the film can be scheduled except the harvest interval, the watering and the weather; everything else takes the station's own planting calendar in whatever order the calendar comes.
place.when_it_looks_best: The first hour after sunrise on a harvest morning, when the low sun comes through the coconut in bars and the beds are being worked from below; and the last hour, when the stakes throw their whole length down the bed. A planting week is worth the wait, because that is the only time the order of the supports is visible as an event rather than as a result: the bare bed, the stakes alone in it, then the cuttings, then the shade. Dry weeks for height and for clean air under the palms; the first week of a rainy spell for the beds filling, for the smell, and for the difference a support makes when it arrives on time.

two_layers.without_the_philosophy: A film about how one leaf crop is actually made. Red soil dug into sunken beds; stakes driven in by hand in a double row; cuttings of an old vine laid at their feet; fronds pulled over the whole bed against the sun; a hose running; manure carried in a basket; a leguminous support tree lopped and its branches laid in the bed it was shading; a vine climbing its own stake to head height; and every third week, hands working upward through the rows taking mature leaves and counting them into bundles of fifty. Overhead, an old coconut plantation with a ruled geometry underneath it that no one on the ground can see. It has a complete shape with nothing said over it, and anyone who likes growing things, or likes work done in an exact order, has a whole piece here.
two_layers.with_the_philosophy: The same fields become the sources' account of what a condition is, filmed in the one place where the conditions are countable, labelled and separately timed. The old analysis refuses both of the easy answers about how anything comes to be: things do not arise by themselves and nobody makes them; they arise from many causes, and the useful question is not what caused this but in what particular way did each thing help. A bed of betel gives every distinction the section needs without arrangement. There is a support that was standing before the thing that needs it. There is a support that arrives afterwards and only keeps going what is already there. There is food, which does not start the plant but carries it for years. There is one thing helping in two ways at once. And there is the hard limit the group's own title can make people forget: the voice never says that everything is connected. It says the books name which thing supports which, in which of twenty-four ways, and list what each kind of support does not reach.

sequence.on_screen: First light, high and looking down through old coconut. The canopy first, then the geometry under it resolving: ruled beds on red soil, thousands of straight stakes in double rows, pale shade cloth over two new plantings, the station's office roof at one edge.
sequence.voice: The second book opens this whole section with a question rather than a doctrine. Do the things this system has just spent seven chapters counting arise by themselves, or are they made by somebody powerful? [C078-M:L3] Its answer is neither. They come about from many causes [C078-M:L5]. What is under these palms is a place that exists to find out how much each cause is worth.

sequence.on_screen: Ground level, a bed being planted. A bare sunken bed, red and empty. A man driving in stakes, a double row of them, a hand and a half apart. Then the bed left exactly like that, stakes and nothing else, for days.
sequence.voice: The first of the twenty-four kinds of help in this part of the text is simply having been there first. What arose earlier supports what arises later, the book says, as a tree that grew first holds up the flowers and the fruit that come afterwards [C082-P:L5723–L5727]. That is what a week of empty bed is. Nothing is growing here yet. The thing it will need is already standing.

sequence.on_screen: Two cuttings of betel laid at the foot of one stake and covered in. Coconut fronds dragged over the whole bed. Then, much later in the same bed, a vine at head height with its stem tied in against the pole.
sequence.voice: Nothing in this bed was grown from seed. Each vine is a cut piece of an older vine with its own short reserve and nothing else. The books' own picture for what happens next is a rice seedling, and it is theirs and not ours: though the strength of the seed is what chiefly makes the plant arise, it is manure and water that chiefly make it grow and keep it standing for months [C075-M:L130]. Food, in this analysis, is not what starts a life. It is what has to keep arriving for one to continue [C075-M:L128; C075-P:L411].

sequence.on_screen: One bed held still, close, with everything in frame at once: the stake, the tied vine, the standing water, the manure worked in at the base, the frond shade overhead, the plot board at the end of the row.
sequence.voice: The other book makes the point with a match. The chemical on the head and the chemical on the side of the box are both conditions of the flame, and they help in different ways; if they helped in the same way, one of them alone would have been enough [C082-M:L3–L5]. Nothing that arises from conditions arises from only one of them [C082-P:L97]. Count what is in this frame. None of it can do another one's work.

sequence.on_screen: A living support tree being lopped back where it has begun to shade the bed it holds up. The cut green branches carried a few feet and laid along the same bed as manure. Then the bare pole standing with the vine still tied to it.
sequence.voice: One thing can help in one way or in several [C082-P:L97]. This tree is holding the vine up, and its branches are about to be its food. And the direction matters more than the connection: the great elements hold up what is derived from them, the book says, and what is derived does not hold them up in return; mind supports the matter it produces, and that matter does not support the mind back [C082-P:L3616–L3620]. The vine leans on this pole. The pole has never needed the vine.

sequence.on_screen: A harvest morning. Hands working upward through the rows, taking mature leaves from the lower stem, counting them into bundles. Water being carried to a bed that has just been cut. Rain arriving across the plantation and the beds filling.
sequence.voice: Then the traffic turns round. What comes later, the text says, keeps up what was already standing, the way water and weather arriving afterwards keep an already-grown tree alive [C082-P:L6055]; and the foods are called foods because they support the repeated arising, the growth and the unbroken continuance of a being, and without them it dies [C082-P:L6843–L6850; C082-P:L6866]. In here the supports are one-way and separately timed, and the whole year's work is the work of keeping each of them coming.

sequence.on_screen: The office end of the day. Plot boards, a field register, a yield figure written against a treatment name. Then back outside: one stake standing with no vine on it, and beside it a vine on a stake that has rotted through at ground level.
sequence.voice: Both books say the same cause and effect was taught at three lengths: very briefly, at middle length, and in full detail [C078-M:L7]. The middle-length telling names only the one principal cause at each step, out of many, and only the one principal result [C078-P:L35]. The detailed one asks through which power, and by which particular kind of help [C078-M:L13]. A yield board carries the brief answer. This field carries the long one. Neither of them is the wrong answer.

sequence.on_screen: Last light down a row, the stakes throwing their full length along the bed. Then height again: the canopy, the ruled ground under it going dark, and the lights of the district's other plots coming on beyond the fence.
sequence.voice: Two corrections before we leave, because this group's name invites both. Warm weather, a good meal, a dry bed: the text counts all of these as strong supports, and it says plainly that they support harm as readily as they support good, and that none of them settles anything by itself [C082-P:L5509–L5527]. And the four foods are not named here as nourishment to be admired. They are named because they are what keeps the round going, and the aim of the passage is its ending [C082-P:L6874].

concept_merge.why_together: C082 carries the film and the other two hold it to its limits. The Paṭṭhāna part gives the exact claims the footage can demonstrate: that a condition-power is a particular manner of helping, argued through the match head and the side of the box, which help differently or else one of them would suffice [C082-M:L3–L5]; that nothing arising from conditions arises from a single one of them, and that one thing may help in one way or several [C082-P:L97]; that prenascence is simply having arisen first, as a tree that grew earlier holds up the flowers that come later [C082-P:L5723–L5727]; that postnascence runs the other way, as water and weather coming afterwards keep an already-grown tree alive [C082-P:L6055]; that the nutriment condition is what makes a continuum arise again, grow and not break off, without which the being dies [C082-P:L6843–L6850; C082-P:L6866]; and that support is directional, since derived matter does not hold up the elements it comes from and mind-born matter does not hold up the mind [C082-P:L3616–L3620]. C075 supplies the source's own agricultural picture, which is the one place in these digests where the distinction between what starts a thing and what sustains it is stated as an image rather than a term: the seed's strength chiefly makes the rice plant arise, while manure and water chiefly make it grow and last for months [C075-M:L130], and 'food' means a cause that, among many, especially brings about and continues a mind-and-body [C075-M:L128; C075-P:L411]. C078 gives the film its frame and its ending: the opening refusal of both self-arising and a maker [C078-M:L3; C078-M:L5], and the three lengths, with the middle one naming only the principal cause at each step [C078-P:L35] and the detailed one naming through which power [C078-M:L13]. A betel bed is where those three meet without being arranged, because its supports are physically separate, individually nameable, put in on different days, and labelled on a board.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That 'many things had to come together' is the weakest possible reading of this material, and that the strong reading is visible in a single bed: the supports are of different kinds, they arrive in an order that cannot be reversed, they help in ways that cannot be substituted, and most of them run one way only. The old version of this idea was a family's paddy season on shared reservoir water. It made a household the subject of a doctrine about conditions, it put a village's water quarrel and a bad year on screen, and it rested the whole chain on an irrigation system, which this slate is not filming again. The concept is unchanged. What has changed is that the supports are now countable without anybody's livelihood being the story: a stake, a shade, a water, a manure, a cutting, and a research board that exists precisely to say what each one is worth when the others are held still.

concept_links.why: Everything on screen is one of this digest's named condition-powers, and the digest's own corrections are the film's closing beat. The match-and-box argument is narrated as the second book's illustration, which is what the digest calls it, and it is used for the one claim it actually makes: that two conditions help in different ways, or one alone would do [C082-M:L3–L5]. The film states out loud that nothing conditioned arises from a single condition and that one thing can help in several ways [C082-P:L97], and it films exactly that in a support tree that is both a pole and, once lopped, a manure. Prenascence is filmed as the week a bed holds stakes and nothing else, on the strength of the digest's own tree-before-the-fruit image [C082-P:L5723–L5727]; postnascence as the water and manure that arrive later and only keep going what is already standing [C082-P:L6055]; the nutriment condition as the year-round carrying of a crop that no food started [C082-P:L6843–L6850; C082-P:L6866]. The directional clause is spoken because the digest insists on it three separate times: derived matter does not support the elements back, and mind-born matter does not support the mind [C082-P:L3616–L3620]. Every 'does not transfer' line that bears on this film is honoured. 'Everything is connected' is refused in the voice, not merely avoided. The passage is not offered as ecology, agronomy or physical causation, and the film says the match is an analogy. The climate-and-food support is given with the digest's own warning that it supports harm as readily as good and settles nothing alone [C082-P:L5509–L5527]. The nutriment material closes on the digest's insistence that these are not wellness nourishment but what keeps the round going [C082-P:L6874]. Predominance, repetition, the grave-act passages and the supernormal-knowledge examples are not used anywhere.

One thing only is taken from this digest, and it is the image the film is built around: the nutriment section's rice seedling, in which the seed's own strength is chief for the plant to arise while manure and water are chief for its growth and its continuance over months [C075-M:L130], together with the section's definition of a food as a cause that, among many causes, especially brings about and keeps up a mind-and-body [C075-M:L128; C075-P:L411]. The film says on screen that this picture is the source's own and that it is a different plant from the one being filmed, since betel is grown from cuttings and never from seed, so the analogy is stated as an analogy rather than smuggled in. The digest's hardest prohibition is respected absolutely: the Pradeepika's tree-of-roots passage, which links good roots in a past life to wealth, honour and qualities and a weak one to living as a servant with barely enough to eat, is not cited, not narrated and not alluded to, and nothing in this film presents any grower's soil, yield, price or circumstances as earned. 'Nutriment' is not used as a wellness slogan; the closing beat says in the sources' own terms that these foods are named because they keep the round going. The faculties, the dominants, the powers, the sex-faculty material and the devotional eight-roots passage are all unused, and no person in the film is offered as an example of any capacity.

This digest gives the film its opening and its last argument. The section's own starting question, whether these things arise by themselves or are made by some powerful being, with the answer that they arise from many causes, is spoken over the first aerial [C078-M:L3; C078-M:L5], which is also how the film honours the slate's non-agency bar without preaching it: there is no maker in the frame and none in the text. The three lengths are given as the digest gives them, with the middle-length telling naming only the principal cause and the principal result at each step [C078-P:L35] and the detailed method naming through which specific power a thing helps, both being needed for a complete account [C078-M:L13; C078-M:L7]. The digest's four 'does not transfer' lines are each honoured: 'everything is connected' is contradicted out loud; 'everything happens for a reason' is excluded by filming a condition as a physical support with no purpose attached; the film never suggests that conditioned things are unreal, only that they are held up; and nothing here is presented as being about moral action and its results, which is a different subject in a different group.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: That in this analysis 'cause' is too coarse a word, and the sharper question is in what particular way each thing helps: some supports have to be standing before the thing that needs them, some arrive afterwards and only keep it going, some feed it for years without having started it, and most of them run in one direction only and cannot do each other's work. The betel bed is an analogy and the film says so; no claim is made about any grower's yield, price or circumstances.
what_must_be_real: The station's own planting calendar, harvest interval and treatments, in their own order. No bed is planted, cleared, shaded, watered or cut for the camera, and no stake is driven in a second time for a better angle. If the only bed available at planting has already had its cuttings put in, the film waits for the next one or loses that beat. Nothing is dressed: a bed with dead vines, a failed treatment, a rotted stake or a plot lost to disease is filmed as it is, and a low yield is not kept off screen. Any smallholder plot outside the fence is filmed only with the occupier's agreement and never as an example of hardship or of anybody's decisions; no price, debt or household circumstance appears. Nobody on the station is asked to confirm any doctrine or to say anything about Abhidhamma, and no worker is made into a character.
position_hint: opening: it is the group's plainest and slowest statement of what a condition is, with the supports countable one at a time and the order visible as an event, and it establishes in the first film that the group's subject is ordered and directional support rather than a web. It hands on the sharper question, in what way did each thing help, to the films that need it. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Letting 'many supports' soften into 'everything is connected', which is the one reading all three digests reject in as many words, and which this group's own title invites.
Pastoral cliche: red soil, low sun and hand work photographed into an idyll, with the crop's real economics and the district's real pressures invisible.
Turning a labelled research plot into a diagram, so that the film becomes an illustrated lecture on twenty-four terms instead of a place.
Letting the vine-and-stake pair read as a lesson about dependence between people, or about who supports whom in a family or a community, which the digests explicitly exclude.
Bringing the Pradeepika's past-merit-and-present-condition material anywhere near the growers, their soil, their yields or their prices.
Turning the nutriment list into a wellness idea, or the match simile into physics or agronomy.
Implying the tradition anticipated plant science, or that a treatment trial is what the texts meant by a condition-power.
Filming a government station as an authority endorsing the film's philosophy, or a worker as a spokesman for it.
Making the shade, the water or the manure look like kindnesses rather than conditions, which would put a giver back into a film whose text has none.
drop_if: The department will not permit the fields, the beds and a harvest to be filmed, since the film is those three things and the canopy above them.
No planting falls inside the filming window and the order of the supports could only be shown by staging a bed, which is the film's second and fifth beats.
Height over the plantation cannot be obtained at all, so the ruled geometry under the canopy, which is the film's first and last image, is unavailable.
The only fields available are smallholdings whose occupiers would become the subject, which is exactly what this rewrite removed.

connections.note: Two films built on a climbing plant: one on a crop whose support was put in before it on purpose, one on a wild length that can be taken hold of anywhere.
One counts the supports of something that is working; the other opens something that has stopped and finds that the single fault was never single.

selection.reason: Its ordinary unit of work, a bed with a stake in it and nothing else yet, is the concept exactly, and the location supplies the whole list of supports already separated, timed and labelled, with no household as the subject.

review.note: Rewritten 2026-09-24 into the footage-led shape. What was dropped: the whole old subject, a single farming household followed through a paddy season on water released from a shared reservoir. Two things were wrong with it. It made a family the subject of a doctrine about conditions, so that a bad year, a water quarrel and a thin harvest would have been on screen as illustrations, and it rested the entire chain on an irrigation system, which this slate is not filming again in any group. The concept is unchanged and is in fact stronger: several supports, none sufficient alone, arriving in a fixed order, each helping in its own particular way. It now comes from a crop whose supports are physically separate objects put in on different days, in a working government station that can consent and has no private life in it. Three digests were re-read from scratch and every citation re-tested against digest evidence rather than carried from the old text; the old idea's concept links were all retested and all three kept, with C082 moved to primary because the condition-powers are what the footage actually shows. The closing beat carries the group's sharpest correction out loud, since C080's digest says twice that 'everything is connected' distorts the source, and C082's and C083's say so again: the film states that the books name which thing supports which, in which way, and in which direction, and that many of these relations run one way only.

suggested_location.name: The Intercropping and Betel Research Station at Dampalassa, Narammala

also_known_as.name: IBRS Narammala
also_known_as.meaning: the Department of Export Agriculture's station for betel and for crops intercropped under coconut, established in 1993

also_known_as.name: kalu bulath
also_known_as.meaning: literally black betel; the thick dark export-grade leaf that this district's beds are grown for, cut at three-week intervals

also_known_as.name: bulath watta
also_known_as.meaning: a betel plot; the sunken-bed enclosure with its rows of stakes

suggested_location.region: Kurunegala District, North Western Province: the laterite and clay-loam coconut lowland of the Narammala area, west of the district capital and inside the country's main betel-growing belt
suggested_location.why_here: Because this is the one place in the country whose ordinary business is the film's question. The station exists to find out what each separate support contributes to a betel vine, and its fields are therefore laid out as countable, labelled, separately timed supports: sunken beds a little over a metre by seven, stakes of living leguminous cuttings or durable dead wood at roughly forty-five centimetre spacing, two betel cuttings at the foot of each stake, shade over a new bed for four to six weeks, then water and manure for years, with harvest every second or third week. That gives the film, without a single arrangement, the prenascent support standing in an empty bed before the thing that needs it; the postnascent support arriving afterwards to keep alive what is already there; food that started nothing and carries everything; and one object helping in two different ways when a live support tree is lopped and its branches laid in the bed it was shading. It is also a working institution rather than a household, in a district where sixty-four acres of it sit under old coconut, so height gives a ruled geometry under a canopy, which is the single most beautiful shot the place produces and also the clearest statement of the concept.
what_to_film: The plantation from height at the start and end of a day, so the canopy resolves into ruled beds, double rows of stakes and pale shade cloth on red soil.
A bed being dug and stakes driven in, then the same bed held for a long beat with stakes and nothing else in it.
The cuttings laid at the foot of the stakes and covered in, and the fronds or netting dragged over the whole bed.
One mature bed in a single held frame with every support in it at once: stake, tied vine, standing water, manure at the base, shade above, plot board at the row end.
A living support tree being lopped where it shades too much, and its cut branches laid along the same bed as green manure.
A harvest morning from below, hands working upward through the rows taking mature leaves and counting them into bundles.
Water arriving: a hose or can along a cut bed, and then real rain across the plantation with the sunken beds filling.
The failures, filmed plainly: a rotted stake under a standing vine, a bed of dead vines, a treatment that did not work, the board that still names it.
Plot boards, the field register and a yield figure written against a treatment name, with no personal details legible.
Smallholder betel beyond the fence at the same hour, only for the fact that the district grows it the same way, and only with the occupier's agreement.
suggested_location.access: By road from the district capital towards the small town the station is named for, and then to the station itself on the Department of Export Agriculture's own land. Everything here depends on written permission from that department: the fields, the store, the plot boards and the register are all theirs, and the station also runs training, so a crew would have to fit a working calendar. Planting and harvest are the department's dates and not the film's. Flying over the plantation needs clearance and the usual civil-aviation permissions, and a canopy that dense means the aerial work has to be planned for the hour when light actually reaches the beds. Any filming outside the fence needs the occupier's own agreement, plot by plot.
suggested_location.best_time: A planting week, chosen against the station's own calendar, since that is the only window in which the order of the supports is an event rather than a result; plus a harvest morning in the same trip, which recurs every second or third week. Within a day, the first hour and the last, when low sun comes through the coconut in bars. Dry weeks for clean air and passable beds; the first days of a rainy spell for the beds filling.

suggested_location.research_note: Desk research only and unverified on the ground. From the sources above: the Intercropping and Betel Research Station was established in 1993 at Narammala as the department's pioneer station for intercropping export agriculture crops under coconut; its stated extent is sixty-four acres including the office complex, research fields and farm; its address is given as Dampalassa, Narammala. On the crop: export-grade betel, called kalu bulath, is commercially confined to a few districts of which this is one, and the laterite and clay-loam soils of this district and its neighbour are described as highly suitable; beds are sunken and roughly 1.2 by 7.5 metres; stakes are set at about 45 by 45 centimetres with two cuttings planted at each stake; supports may be live plants of a quick-growing leguminous tree or durable dead wood; new beds are shaded with coconut fronds or other material for about four to six weeks; harvest is at three-week intervals for export and two for the local market. The coordinates given here are a direction towards the Narammala and Dampalassa area, not a survey of the station gate, and no field, bed or plot has been identified. Nobody has been approached and no permission has been sought. Three things the film depends on are inferences rather than confirmed facts about this station: that live leguminous supports are used here and are lopped back into the beds as green manure, that a planting can be caught inside a filming window, and that plot boards and a field register exist in a form legible on camera. No photograph of the station, its fields or any of its beds was found on Wikimedia Commons; the one image is of a betel plant on a support elsewhere.

unknowns: Whether the Department of Export Agriculture will open a research station, its fields and its records to a film crew at all.
Whether a planting can be filmed inside the window, since the order of the supports is the film's argument and cannot be staged.
Whether live leguminous supports are actually used at this station, and whether their loppings go back into the same beds.
Whether height can be flown over the plantation, and whether enough light reaches the beds under old coconut for the aerial to read as a geometry.
Whether the station's own trials would put a named researcher's work on screen in a way the department would object to.
Whether anything outside the fence is needed at all, and if so whether occupiers will agree to be filmed without becoming the subject.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. The location is proposed by Claude from desk research and is unverified. No scene or shot is decided here.
